# Preparing the node-visit full-chain semantic comparison

This is **source only**. The Chair has released preparation and synthetic source checks. Compilation and full-chain execution remain unreleased. There is no timing, profiler, public-selection or ABI-change entry point. The whole product remains **open — awaiting merge**.

The existing preparation/unit runner and frozen `extrema_screen` admission run unchanged before every new stage. They preserve all qualified Go/go.mod bytes, closed ignored/untracked Go inventory, six AR exclusions, original 14/6 overlays and historical native/GoJS proofs. The new full-chain baseline is current e492 under exactly six exclusions; the candidate adds only the admitted one-line `.source` envelope replacement. Both sides use the unchanged opt-in 27-case recorder and current screen test bytes. All new snapshots of physical Go files gain `.source` suffixes.

## Intended build and execution after separate review

The source producer can prepare a fresh native pair and two actual GoJS/WASM modules using Go 1.26.10 and its already qualified `wasm_exec.js`, pinned Node 26.12.0, one compiler process at a time, exact effective target/overlay/environment records, and conservative effective source sets. Every new runner/source payload is frozen and hashed. Each module is capped at 16 MiB; each compile has a 25-second supervisor limit. Reusing an existing build ID refuses to overwrite evidence.

After another execution release, run each backend and each of the five closed rates (8/44.1/48/96/192 kHz). Every invocation runs exactly one baseline child and one candidate child. Both outputs must match each other and the corresponding accepted **e492 candidate** archive for that backend/rate. The old original/extrema pair and all its modules remain untouched. Native and WASM are compared within their own backend; the known cross-target numeric-state digest differences remain UNPROVEN.

The existing recorder retains its 200,000 base-frame, 800,000 high-rate-frame upper, 16 Mi numeric-word, 8 MiB output, and 2 MiB graph-object bounds, with its conservative 6 MiB scratch/preparation allowance. Go tests retain 25-second timeouts; execution parents retain 28-second watchdogs and 256 KiB logs. The existing closed filesystem and post-exit lifecycle helpers are imported unchanged. These are work/output bounds, not runtime RSS limits.

Every parent validates Go counters, byte counts, output mode/hash, process/cleanup status and source/module/overlay/runtime receipts. The final seal re-reads actual pair/archive bytes plus original logs and parent/child receipts across all five rates: 135 cases per side for each backend. Failures retain raw partial output and exclusive receipts.

```sh
# SOURCE admission only; authorized now.
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit_graph/producer.py admit

# The following intended commands require separate Chair build/execution releases.
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit_graph/producer.py build NEW_ID
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit_graph/run-pair.py native NEW_ID 8000
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit_graph/run-pair.py wasm NEW_ID 8000
# Repeat each backend for 44100, 48000, 96000 and 192000, then re-read/seal proof.
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit_graph/run-pair.py seal NEW_ID
```

Original alias, partition, tail, wrap, repeat/reset, capacity and no-allocation contract gates remain separately required before any timing. Source checks, module builds and finite byte equality do not release timing. The prior steady 192 kHz candidate means remain above 0.666666667 ms per 128 frames. Historical race/Node failures, transparency failures, Newton limitation, unqualified AR work and all earlier timing data remain retained; public activation and browser continuity remain open.
